disposition_reason: Primary ICP-OES occurrence data for Cd, Pb, Al and Ni in 50 apiary honeys of five varieties from urbanized vs ecologically pure areas of Podkarpackie, Poland, with soil-plant-bee-honey transfer comparisons usable as apiary-siting controls.
disposition_locator: Methods 'Honey samples' (journal p. 49); Table 2 (p. 53); Table 3 (p. 54); Results 'Honey contamination by toxic metals' and 'Heavy metals transfer' (pp. 53-54)

study.design: apiary sampling (soil-plant-bee-honey transfer study, urbanized vs ecological habitat)
study.material_scope: Honey from 10 local apiaries (5 urbanized U, 5 ecologically pure E); 10 each of dandelion, rapeseed, goldenrod, tilia and honeydew honey; variety assigned by beekeeper from nectar-flow availability
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Produced at the sampled apiaries in Podkarpackie (Podkarpacie) region, south-eastern Poland; not retail purchases.
study.sampling_unit: honey samples (one per variety per apiary); analyses in triplicate
study.method: ICP-OES (Thermo iCAP 6500) after microwave mineralization (1 g sample + 8 mL conc. HNO3, Milestone Ethos Ultrawave-One); Y and Yb internal standards
study.lod_loq: 'detection threshold for each element was at least 0.01 mg/kg' (single statement for all elements); LOQ not reported
study.basis: Ambiguous: Methods say results are 'mg per kg for honey' (vs d.w. for soil/plants/bees), but Table 2 caption labels bee and honey values 'mg/kg d.w.'. Recorded as printed; treated as honey as analysed unless resolved.
study.qa: CRM NIST-1515 (apple leaves) used for validation (results not reported); targeted repeatability RSD 20%; recovery 97-102%; calibration fit >0.99; triplicate analyses.

controls.control: Apiary habitat: urbanized (U) vs ecologically pure (E) area
controls.comparator: Same honey variety from 5 U apiaries vs 5 E apiaries (one-way ANOVA + Tukey)
controls.outcome: Honey metal content from E and U areas was 'comparable'; abstract: influence of human activity (region development) not significant (p>0.05). Significant E-U differences in honey only for Al in dandelion honey (E 8.13 vs U 1.72 mg/kg, E higher), Ni in goldenrod (E 0.08 vs U 0.55) and tilia (E 0.17 vs U 0.63) honey (U higher), and Mn in tilia honey (E 2.22 vs U 0.90). No significant E-U difference for honey Cd or Pb.
controls.locator: Abstract; Table 2 superscripts a/b (journal p. 53); Results 'Honey contamination by toxic metals' (pp. 53-54)

controls.comparator: Soil pH (U 4.6 +/- 1.0 vs E 5.2 +/- 1.1) and metal migration along the chain
controls.outcome: Abstract states migration of heavy metals, especially Cd, in the soil-plant-bee-honey chain was accelerated by soil acidity (p<0.05). The supporting correlation statistics are not tabulated in the paper. Soil total metals did not differ significantly between E and U (p>0.05).

controls.control: Bee body as a biological barrier between forage and honey
controls.comparator: Soil vs plants vs bee bodies vs honey (Table 3 pooled means)
controls.outcome: Cd: soil 0.37, plants 0.40, bees 0.63, honey 0.02 mg/kg (honey significantly lower). Pb: soil 21.30 > plants 0.52 > bees 0.13 > honey 0.05 mg/kg, each step significant. Al and Ni were comparable in bees and honey (Al 12.59 vs 11.64; Ni 0.34 vs 0.45), so bees are not a barrier for Al/Ni. Authors conclude bees bioaccumulate Cd and Pb and block their transfer to honey.
controls.locator: Table 3 (journal p. 54); Results 'Heavy metals transfer in the studied food chain' (p. 54); Conclusions (p. 55)

controls.control: Forage plant species (Cd-accumulating plants near the apiary)
controls.comparator: Bioaccumulation factor (plant/soil) by species and area
controls.outcome: Goldenrod and dandelion are Cd accumulators (BF>=1: goldenrod 1.23 E / 2.20 U; dandelion 1.64 E / 1.26 U); rapeseed least (0.38 / 0.57). Plant BF was not reflected in honey: goldenrod honey Cd 0.02 mg/kg in both areas. Authors produced maps of high soil-to-plant migration areas as a tool for local beekeepers.
controls.locator: Table 4 and Figure 1 (journal p. 55); Results p. 54

controls.comparator: Honeydew vs dandelion, goldenrod, rapeseed, tilia honeys
controls.outcome: Variety mattered more than habitat: honeydew honey had higher Al (47.00-54.37 mg/kg means) and Mn; rapeseed honey was highest in Ni. Both Pb exceedances of the Polish 0.30 mg/kg limit stated in the text were honeydew samples.
controls.locator: Table 2 (journal p. 53); Results 'Honey contamination by toxic metals' (pp. 53-54)

controls.control: Polish maximum levels for honey (Minister of Health 2003): Cd 0.03 mg/kg, Pb 0.30 mg/kg
controls.outcome: Text: Cd exceeded in '5% of the samples (2 honeydew, 2 dandelion and 1 tilia)' - 5 of 50 is 10%; Pb exceeded in 2 honeydew samples. Table 2 maxima suggest additional exceedances not mentioned in the text (dandelion E Pb max 0.40 > 0.30; goldenrod U Cd max 0.04 > 0.03).
controls.locator: Results 'Honey contamination by toxic metals', journal p. 54; Table 2 (p. 53)

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary repeats the paper's statement that 5% of honeys exceeded the 0.03 mg/kg Cd limit, 'two honeydew, two dandelion, and one tilia' - 5 of 50 samples is 10%, an internal inconsistency in the primary that the summary does not flag.

Stored summary says only two honeydew samples exceeded the 0.30 mg/kg Pb limit; primary Table 2 prints a dandelion (E) Pb max of 0.40 mg/kg, which also exceeds 0.30 mg/kg. Similarly goldenrod (U) Cd max 0.04 mg/kg exceeds 0.03 mg/kg but is not among the listed Cd exceedances.
Stored summary lists metals as Cd, Pb, Al, Mn, Ni; the primary Methods say Cd, Pb, Hg, Al, Ni were determined, but no Hg results appear and Mn is reported instead. The summary does not note this.
Stored summary omits that a CRM (NIST-1515) was used for validation.
Stored summary's honey table values match the primary Table 2 cell-for-cell (no numeric contradictions found).
unresolved: Year and months of honey collection are not stated (bees were sampled June-July; honey timing unstated); collection_period left null.
Basis ambiguity: Table 2 caption says honey values are mg/kg d.w., but Methods say honey results are 'mg per kg' (implying as-analysed). Not resolvable from the text.

Per-cell n is not printed; n=5 inferred from design. Several cells are arithmetically impossible for 5 single values (e.g., honeydew U Pb mean 0.09 with max 0.77; dandelion E Al mean 8.13 with max 46.16; dandelion U Al mean 1.72 with max 10.29), suggesting the cells may summarise replicate measurements or a different n.
Table 3 honey Ni max (2.43 mg/kg) and Mn max (16.72 mg/kg) exceed every corresponding Table 2 honey maximum; Table 3 Cd min 0.00 conflicts with Table 2 minima (>=0.01) and text range (0.01-0.07).
Hg is listed as determined in Methods but no Hg results are reported anywhere.
How values below the 0.01 mg/kg threshold were treated (printed as 0.00) is not stated; zeros were not converted to numeric zeros in this extraction.
Mn results (Table 2/3) are not extracted as findings because Mn is outside the schema analyte list; they are cited only in notes/controls.
